record_before.summary: Municipality must authorize multifamily and mixed-use residential in areas zoned commercial, industrial or mixed use (and some public/religious land) if at least 40% of rental units are affordable (s. 420.0004) for 30 years; no zoning change required; density, FAR and height floors apply.
record_before.effective_date_note: SB 102 effective 2023-07-01; SB 328 effective 2024-05-16; SB 1730 effective 2025-07-01
record_before.tax_exemption_note: Fla. Stat. 196.1978(3)(d)1: 75% of assessed value exempt for units at 80-120% AMI; units at or below 80% AMI exempt from ad valorem taxes. 196.1979 (cited earlier) is the separate local-option exemption.
record_before.statutory_exclusions_note: 166.04151(7)(o): airport-impacted areas (s. 333.03), Wekiva Study Area, Everglades Protection Area, working waterfronts, open-character districts, areas of critical state concern; developments within 1/4 mile of a military installation may not be administratively approved. TRPA is not in the statute.

summary: Checked against the official text of Fla. Stat. 166.04151 and the Florida Senate page for SB 102. Confirmed: the 40% / 30-year affordability rule, the density, FAR and height floors, the SB 102 effective date of 7/1/2023, and Ch. 2023-17. Wrong: commercial_or_industrial_only=true, because government-owned and religious land qualify regardless of zoning; statutory_exclusions, which includes TRPA (not in the statute) and omits several exclusions; and session/bill history, which leaves out the 2026 amendments (ch. 2026-14, 2026-163, 2026-179). The short_name cites 196.1979 while statute_citation cites 196.1978. Unverified because the tool limit was reached: s. 196.1978 tax-exemption details, the s. 420.0004 income ceiling, and the SB 328 and SB 1730 effective dates.
